ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal straight line, and a line segment inclined upward to the right intersects the horizontal line on the left side. On the left there is an inverted triangle; its left horizontal vertex is marked 50°, its bottom vertex is marked 78°, and its right vertex is exactly the intersection point of the slanted line and the horizontal line. Angle 2 is marked above this intersection point, in the position of the vertical angle paired with the unknown angle at the intersection point of the inverted triangle on the left. Reasoning: The sum of the three interior angles of the inverted triangle on the left is 180°, so the third interior angle at the intersection point is 180° - 50° - 78° = 52°. Angle 2 and this 52° angle are vertical angles; vertical angles are equal, therefore angle 2 = 52°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle 2$ in the figure.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a horizontal line intersected by a slanted segment on the left. The small inverted triangle on the left has two labeled interior angles, 50° at the left horizontal vertex and 78° at the bottom vertex. Use the triangle angle sum to find its third angle at the shared intersection: 180° - 50° - 78° = 52°. This third angle is vertically opposite to angle 2 at the same intersection of the slanted segment and horizontal line, so angle 2 also measures 52°.
